concepts.description: The connection setup procedure TCP uses to establish a session between two endpoints before any data is exchanged.
concepts.name: Three-Way Handshake

concepts.description: TCP's mechanism for adjusting the sending rate to avoid overloading the network, using slow start, congestion avoidance, and fast recovery.
concepts.name: Congestion Control

concepts.description: TCP's guarantee that segments arrive reliably and in order, presented to the application as a continuous byte stream.
concepts.name: Reliable Ordered Byte-Stream Delivery

concepts.description: TCP's mechanism for preventing a sender from overwhelming a receiver, governed by the receiver's advertised window.
concepts.name: Flow Control

concepts.description: The core principles of the Transmission Control Protocol, covering how connections are established, how data is delivered, and how traffic is regulated. This document treats them as the foundation for understanding TCP behavior.
concepts.name: Tcp Fundamentals

concepts.description: A congestion control phase in which the sender rapidly increases its congestion window to probe available network capacity.
concepts.name: Slow Start

concepts.description: A congestion control phase in which the sender grows its congestion window more gradually after slow start to avoid causing congestion.
concepts.name: Congestion Avoidance

concepts.description: The receive buffer space the receiver reports to the sender, which limits how much unacknowledged data the sender may transmit.
concepts.name: Advertised Window

concepts.description: A congestion control technique that reduces the sending rate after duplicate acknowledgments without fully restarting slow start.
concepts.name: Fast Recovery
